A dead orchard in strict rows, bare black fruit-trees lacquered with ice, every branch a silver filigree against white sky, fallen fruit glazed under frost like forgotten jewels.
A topiary hedge maze under deep frost, the clipped beasts half-collapsed into bare armatures, ice-dusted corridors narrowing into shadow, the whole labyrinth silent and exquisitely menacing.
A long ice-glazed arbor walk, climbing roses frozen into grey lattice overhead, the pergola tunnel stretching endlessly, every tendril a crystal wire, frost-light pooling blue along the stone floor.
A sunken grotto garden, mossy stone walls glazed with black ice, dead ferns draping the niches, a cracked urn tipped sideways, frost feathering every surface in cold silver lace.
A walled black-rose garden at dusk, thousands of thorned stems bare and black against old stone, frost-rimed arbors casting thin shadows, the air bitter, beautiful, and utterly forsaken.
A frozen fountain court ringed by iron railings, the great cascade locked in translucent ice columns, stone basins heaped with frozen leaves, the courtyard perfectly still beneath a pewter sky.
A weeping-statuary garden of draped stone figures, each shrouded form silver with frost, positioned along a cracked path between dead yew hedges, their bowed heads heavy with mourning and ice.

A derelict glass greenhouse, ribbed iron frame intact but panes shattered in rows, frost feathering the remaining glass, dead orchids brown and collapsed within, exquisitely ruinous under cold grey light.
A dead orchard where gnarled black apple trees line a frost-heaved path, their bare crowns tangled against a white sky, ice on every twig, mournful and still as painted grief.
A topiary maze of frost-dusted beasts, their shapes half-devoured by winters of neglect, bare branches threading the cut forms, grey corridors between walls of frozen hedge leading nowhere.

An ice-glazed pergola walk, iron arches mantled in frozen wisteria, each cluster a frozen chandelier overhead, the long stone-flagged tunnel stretching into cold grey distance, achingly beautiful and abandoned.
A sunken grotto-garden, tomb-slabs rising from frost-blackened moss, stone urns overturned among dead ivy, the grotto mouth dark and wet with ice, cold silence heaped like snow over everything.
A winter cloister garth, the frozen courtyard garden ringed by a stone arcade, dead box hedges forming a cross-pattern under frost, a cracked sundial at center, the cloister shadow absolute and cold.

A frozen lily-pond garden, the black water glazed solid, dead reed-stems piercing the ice in rows, a mossy stone bridge arching over the stillness, bare willows trailing frozen fingers across the surface.
A walled black-rose garden under heavy snowfall, thorned canes bent white, the iron gate open and rusting, frost-rimed petals black against snow, every arbor a dark gothic arch of thorns.

A frozen fountain court at night, moonlight refracting through ice columns in cold prisms, the stone pool a mirror of frost, the surrounding clipped hedges furred white, unbearably lonely and glittering.
A weeping-statuary garden where moss-bearded angels kneel in a circle, each figure frost-silvered, their open stone palms holding ice, black yew surrounding them, the whole scene still as held grief.

A derelict glass conservatory, frost writing fern-patterns across intact panes, dead bougainvillea collapsed in rust-colored drifts within, the iron door hanging open, cold air and silence equally dense inside.
A dead orchard at the edge of a frozen field, the trees black and bare, their crooked limbs interlocked overhead, frost thick on every surface, the long rows receding into cold fog.
A topiary garden of frost-devoured peacock and lion forms, their once-clipped shapes now wild and skeleton-bare, ice glazing every twig, the garden floor a patchwork of frost and dead leaf.

A sunken grotto garden, black water seeping between frost-glazed stone steps, dead moss silver on every surface, cracked classical figures half-buried in the banks, the cold air smelling of stone and winter.
